correctness.rationale: An irredundant factor must miss a special gap in 14–27; covering that interval also excludes every smaller positive integer because it has a positive multiple in the interval. The symmetric/pseudo-symmetric characterization plus testing closure up to the Frobenius number gives exactly the relevant factors. Independent enumeration gives 285 factors and 163 distinct masks. The 8,788 three-mask unions (allowing repeats) cover at most 13 positions, excluding all lengths at most three. A descending subset DP over distinct factors gives 56 four-covers, 28 of each stated Frobenius multiset. Each of the seven A masks has two realizations, B and D each have two choices, and C is unique. All products cover; the roles remain distinguishable in the repeated-27 case. Since triples cannot cover, all 56 are irredundant. In reading the pair-join description, the intended rule is two consecutive pairs in sorted index order (j < k), as in the frozen code; lexicographic order of pairs alone would not ensure uniqueness.
residual_risks: The independent computation exhausts this fixed H28 claim, not all multiplicities or all irreducible-decomposition lengths.

value.rationale: H28 is selected by a published construction's first failure, not an arbitrary cutoff. The exact extremal census resolves whether alternative shortest factorizations exist and determines all overlaps in Frobenius profiles, including a repeated Frobenius number, with a small fully explicit family and a lower-bound certificate. This is useful as a test case for shortest-decomposition methods and is more than rechecking one known example.
residual_risks: The value is a fixed-object structural classification, not a uniform theorem about larger ordinary semigroups.
